criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-cli --test external_calls`: land_pr_with_a_one_off_500_on_each_call_is_retried_and_lands ends Landed; the fake host's check run in crates/athena-cli/tests/external_calls.rs is named 'fmt, clippy, tests'.
criteria.evidence: Ran it: 11 passed, including land_pr_with_a_one_off_500_on_each_call_is_retried_and_lands. The diff at external_calls.rs:92 shows the fake's reply as {"name": "fmt, clippy, tests", "status": "completed", "conclusion": "success"}, with no id. So the test also shows that the classifier does not need an id.

criteria.criterion: Grep of crates/**/tests*.rs, tests/ and *_tests.rs for check_runs fakes shows no check run without a name; every fake carries 'fmt, clippy, tests' or is intentionally another name.
criteria.evidence: I used the Grep tool for `check_runs|check-runs` over crates/**/*.rs. The test fakes are external_calls.rs:92 (named) and, in gh/tests.rs, :93 and :2266 (both required_green_reply(), named EARLY_RUN_JOB), :683/:689 (named), :712 and the Reporting fake (built from required_run/head_run, both named), and :1737 (already named). The only unnamed run is the deliberate `unnamed` case in the new table test, which checks that an unnamed run cannot decide. Other hits are production code or are not check-run fakes (run/mod.rs, state.rs). The conclusion fakes in run/tests.rs are workflow-run jobs, and they are named.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core gh`: a PR whose required check 'fmt, clippy, tests' is green and an optional check (the pull request head) is red is reported landed or waiting, never failed, with a note in the report warnings; a red required check is still Red and a missing or pending required check stays Pending.
criteria.evidence: Ran it: 104 passed. That includes only_the_required_check_decides_and_optional_failures_become_notes (cases i–viii plus unnamed), an_optional_red_check_reaches_the_report_as_a_warning_and_the_job_lands (Landed, checks Green, one 'pull request head' warning), an_optional_red_check_with_the_setting_off_leaves_the_pull_request_waiting_and_green (Open, Green, warning present), a_red_required_check_is_still_red_and_nothing_is_merged, and a_missing_required_check_stays_pending_and_nothing_is_merged. On the base, the any-failure rule would have made cases (i) and (v) and the Landed test Red.

criteria.criterion: The optional-check notes come from the same check-runs and status read as the verdict (one classify call returning both); Grep of the diff shows no second check_runs_reply or status_reply call for notes.
criteria.evidence: client.rs:417-431: check_report makes one GET of check-runs and one GET of status, then one classify_checks call that returns CheckReport{checks, notes}. checks() wraps check_report. The diff has no check_runs_reply, status_reply or optional_failures. The test the_verdict_and_the_notes_come_from_one_read_of_the_check_runs_and_the_status passes; it asserts one read of each path and 2 paths in total. In early.rs, wait_for_checks takes the notes from the same read as the verdict it keeps.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-gate`: a commit adding a held job's records with no verification passes classify_pre_merge, and a commit adding a finished job's closing records with no verification still returns Uncovered::NoVerification.
criteria.evidence: Ran it: 123 passed, including the_records_of_a_held_job_are_records_only_and_need_no_verification (Ok, RecordsOnly, job None) and the_closing_records_of_a_finished_job_without_a_verification_are_still_refused (Err(NoVerification(job))). Candidate2 writes candidate.json (records.rs:2809-2810), which is in closing_jobs' CLOSING list. So on the base, the held commit would have counted as a landing and been refused, which means the new test fails without the change.

criteria.criterion: CHANGELOG.md has an entry describing both fixes (required-checks-only judgment; held-job records pass the pull request head check).
criteria.evidence: The new entry under Fixed names both fixes and the root cause of each: classify_checks counted every run and status, and closing_jobs counted a held job as a landing. It also states the limit (CI with no job of that name reads as pending) and points to D149. It is written for an outside reader.

findings.summary: A test comment names the wrong file: it says 'candidate2.json', but the record is written as candidate.json (schema athena.candidate/2).
findings.evidence: The comment says "the candidate (`candidate2.json`)". records.rs:2809-2810 maps AnyRecord::Candidate2 to `{dir}/candidate.json`.

findings.summary: The required check name is hard-coded. A repository whose CI has no 'fmt, clippy, tests' job now reads as pending forever and never lands. This limit is documented in D149, and reading branch protection is listed as a follow-up.
findings.evidence: In this repo, ci.yml:403-406 defines `name: fmt, clippy, tests` with `if: always()` on both push and pull_request, so the name is correct here. The limit is stated in the CHANGELOG and in D149's Assumption and Follow-ups.

summary: The change does what was asked. The fake host in crates/athena-cli/tests/external_calls.rs now names its check run 'fmt, clippy, tests', and land_pr_with_a_one_off_500_on_each_call_is_retried_and_lands ends Landed (I ran the tests: 11/11 pass). I searched every *.rs file for check-run fakes. Every one now carries a name: gh/tests.rs FakeRunner and Refusing use required_green_reply(), and the new tests use either the required name or a deliberately optional one ('pull request head', 'other'). The one unnamed run left is deliberate: a test showing that an unnamed run never decides. classify_checks now judges only the run named CI_AGGREGATE_JOB. It returns a CheckReport whose verdict and optional-failure notes come from one read of check-runs and one read of status, and a test checks that exactly 2 paths were requested. land_pr adds the notes to the report's warnings. closing_jobs leaves out held jobs (candidate, no verification, no outcome), and a finished job with no verification still gives NoVerification. The athena-core gh tests (104 pass), the athena-gate tests (123 pass) and the refusal corpus (7 pass) all pass in this snapshot. ci.yml confirms that a job named 'fmt, clippy, tests' runs with if: always() on both push and pull_request, so the required name is real. Every changed file is on the deliverables list. The only finding is a nit in a test comment.
